# mdk guide — getting started

## Requirements

- machin >= 0.142 on PATH (or $MACHIN)
- C compiler
- cmake (first run builds vendored SDL3 3.4.20)
- FreeType + HarfBuzz dev packages (pkg-config freetype2 harfbuzz)
- OpenGL 3.3
- an X11/Wayland display (DISPLAY=:0)

Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt install build-essential cmake pkg-config libfreetype-dev libharfbuzz-dev libgl-dev libx11-dev`

## Steps

```
git clone https://github.com/javimosch/machin-desktop && cd machin-desktop
./mdk new apps/hello     # writes apps/hello/app.src
./mdk dev apps/hello     # window opens; edits redraw in place, state kept
./mdk build apps/hello -o hello   # release binary
```

First run builds vendored SDL3 3.4.20 statically (~1 min).

## The starter app

```
func view() {
    n := state_int("count", 0)
    col()
    fill()
    center()
    gap(16.0)
        text(str(n), 56.0)
        bold()
        row()
        gap(10.0)
            if button("Increment") { set_int("count", n + 1) }
            if button_ghost("Reset") { set_int("count", 0) }
        end()
    end()
}
```

## Three ideas

1. `view()` rebuilds the whole tree every frame it runs (input, resize, reload, or `animate()`); idle apps run no frames.
2. State lives in the host store (`state_int`/`set_int`, `state_f`/`set_f`, `state_str`/`set_str`) and survives reloads. MFL globals reset on reload and must not be reassigned every frame.
3. Widgets return this frame's event: `if button("Save") { ... }`. Hit-testing uses last frame's layout.

## App contract

1. An app is a directory of .src files. mdk prepends framework/*.src and compiles them together with machin (encode concatenates files: that is the module system).
2. Define exactly one `func view()`. It runs every frame that needs drawing (input, resize, reload, or animate()).
3. Do not define main(). The framework exports mdk_frame, which wraps view() in arena { } so a frame's temporaries are freed when it returns.
4. Keep state in the host store: state_int/set_int, state_f/set_f, state_str/set_str. It survives every hot reload; MFL globals do not (they reset on reload).
5. Never assign per-frame values to MFL globals: inside the frame arena, a global assignment promotes the value out of it and leaks every frame. Assigning a global once (a cache filled on first frame) is fine.
6. Build the UI top-down every frame: open containers with col()/row(), add content, close with end(). Modifiers (gap, bg, pad, ...) apply to the LAST created element, or to the container just closed by end().
7. Widgets return their event for this frame: if button("Save") { ... }.

## Commands

- `./mdk new <appdir>` — scaffold an app directory with app.src (a counter)
- `./mdk dev <appdir>` — build the app as a .so, open the window, rebuild on every save; the window and state survive; build errors draw over the last good frame
- `./mdk build <appdir> [-o out]` — one release binary with the app linked in (no reload, sleeps when idle)
- `./mdk shot <appdir> out.ppm [--size W H] [--frames N] [--click X Y]...` — render N frames (clicks are real SDL events) and save a screenshot; convert out.ppm out.png to view
- `./mdk check <appdir>` — typecheck the app with the framework (machin encode), no window
- `./mdk guide` — print this JSON

## Verify without a human

- `./mdk check <app>` — typecheck only
- `./mdk shot <app> out.ppm --click X Y` — real SDL clicks, then screenshot; `convert out.ppm out.png`
- during `mdk dev`: `kill -USR1 <mdk-host pid>` saves the frame to `$MDK_SHOT` (default /tmp/mdk-shot.ppm)
